value.policy: VM entry/normal-return checks; synchronous computation; ordinary JSON output obeys the existing per-value UTF-8 allocation ceiling (trap 14) Native bytes.to_str, bytes.from_str, bytes.concat, str.concat and str.slice now admit covered output and temporary payload capacity before conversion/copy; retained string/byte aliases preserve charges. Capacity rejection maps to allocation trap 14. UTF-8 decode discards invalid-input exceptions within temporary admission before returning the conversion error. String concat measures UTF-8 size without encoded copies and checks cancellation every 4096 code points; conversion/copy calls themselves remain synchronous with no intra-call preemption. Integer formatting, implicit copies and other unrelated producers remain separate accounting work. Structural equality compares charged and plain string/byte scalars by their language value before checking differing union member types; ownership wrappers do not introduce new language scalar types. Native JSON decoding now admits scalar payloads, parser containers and typed destinations through the shared budget; owned aliases retain their reservations. Scans check cancellation periodically, typed traversal and container operations check at boundaries, and numeric/scanner calls remain synchronous. Typed recursion errors map to conversion depth errors. Generic parser metadata and Python object headers are outside payload accounting. Structural equality and union matching preserve declared integer widths across ownership subclasses. Money/time validators and VM arithmetic retain declared integer width checks while accepting ownership subclasses. Parallel limits accept owned i64 values; buffer sizes/ranges preserve the strict ledger counter representation.

clock_entropy_secret.policy: VM boundary checks around synchronous host access

sleep.policy: shared remaining budget, requested waits <=50 ms

log.policy: synchronous stderr write/flush; partial output possible

file.policy: Context checkpoints around synchronous file operations and bounded read chunks; partial writes possible. Read scratch and final output copy reserve the shared native-byte budget; budget exhaustion traps 14. Parent traversal and target descriptors reserve shared capacity before open and retain ownership through physical close; descriptor exhaustion also traps 14; host calls are not preemptible within a syscall.

limiter.policy: timed state-lock admission; admitted token consumption completes

observation.policy: timed observation-lock admission; terminal telemetry may be omitted

storage.policy: timed locks and prepublication checkpoints; entered replacement cleanup completes; opt-in authority lock consumes Store/VM admission budget; snapshot hashing is synchronous; authority advancement, receipts and exact staged recovery retain commit ambiguity and complete admitted durability work before return Version-2 authority checks the active writer identity after store/authority lock acquisition, including no-op mutations; trusted fence-key advances ciphertext and writer policy through the same admitted publication boundary. Initial host migration uses the same deadline for store and recovery-copy locks, synchronous SQLite integrity/encryption checks, recovery-copy durability before active publication, and the existing admitted active publication barrier. VM-context storage directory, lock, snapshot, key-file, authority, receipt, migration recovery and staging descriptors reserve shared capacity before acquisition. Descriptor exhaustion maps to DbError; admitted durability semantics remain unchanged. Physical cleanup is synchronous; ambiguous close retains a quarantined charge. Host callers without a resource context are outside this accounting. VM-context snapshot reads use admitted scratch and charged immutable payloads, with cancellation checks before and after each read. Input aliases retain charges. Non-VM reads retain their prior bounded behavior. VM-context normal loads and anchored restore decrypt into preadmitted plaintext; saves admit framed ciphertext and nonce capacity before encryption. Scoped memoryviews avoid nonce/ciphertext slicing copies. Keyring failures clear destination bytes before fallback; scoped output is cleared on exit, with retained aliases preserving charges. Cipher calls and 4096-byte-chunk clearing remain synchronous; no intra-call preemption guarantee is made. VM saves validate the private main database page count and page size before serialization, admitting an owned image and two temporary image capacities before calling serialize. No writes intervene between size measurement and serialization. A writable memoryview copies the result into the owned buffer; temporary bytes are cleared before temporary reservation release. Owned image aliases retain their charge through publication and subsequent retention. Cancellation is checked before serialize and after copying; SQLite calls and the copy are synchronous with no intra-call preemption guarantee. SQLite deserialization storage and native library allocator usage remain outside these payload reservations. The maintenance CLI now keeps a shared payload budget and descriptor registry alive across each command, with validated nonnegative i64 limits (defaults 256 MiB payload capacity and 256 descriptors). Restore reads through an owned file-input path with admission before bounded reads, cancellation checks around reads, and charged aliases through restore and hashing. The existing exact-bytes host API remains compatible but does not retroactively admit caller allocation. Registry cleanup runs on every command exit including interruption; incomplete cleanup reports failure. Maintenance contexts impose no overall deadline; existing store lock deadlines and admitted durability semantics still apply.

outbound.policy: 8192-byte URL and 1 MiB body/model JSON payload limits before transport; shared budget includes preparation and bounded model serialization; inherited VM context; DNS remains synchronous Socket admission precedes each connection attempt; capacity failure maps to HttpError/ModelError. One descriptor charge follows TLS transfer and survives logical connection close until the final response reader releases it. Failed transfer closes the current owner and disarms any untransferred TLS alias. DNS, trust-store access and native TLS allocations remain outside this descriptor policy. Model request envelopes use owned JSON byte chunks and a charged final payload. Model and HTTP responses use readinto scratch with checks before/after each read, bounded chunks and admitted final copies. Returned HTTP bytes retain their charge across VM and host aliases. Request.data is cleared on model-call exit; retained byte aliases retain their reservations. Model-response UTF-8 decoding admits temporary and owned Unicode capacity while input bytes remain charged, using the inherited deadline checks. Invalid UTF-8 preserves the ModelError network result. Model-response JSON parsing now uses admitted scalar/container producers and the inherited remaining-deadline check; returned text retains its own reservation after the response graph is dropped. JSON capacity rejection maps to allocation trap 14. Transport-internal copies remain separate accounting work.

local_provider.policy: synchronous trusted companion, no context transfer; restricted VMs reject

evolution.policy: Minimum wave/VM budget for preparation and apply admission; child reaping and admitted journal completion precede owned staging cleanup. Cleanup may exceed the budget; primary exceptions survive cleanup failure, and abrupt parent death may leave staging.

serving.policy: serving/request budgets capped by 10-second connection lifetime and 100-request quota; bounded response serialization; FIFO connection queue with explicit fairness limits; drain/abort then join; service-token requests reload the pinned private file with context checks before/after synchronous reading; invalid/unavailable credentials fail closed before handler admission; already admitted requests retain context Listener and accepted sockets reserve shared descriptor capacity before acquisition. Listener exhaustion maps to ListenError. Accept exhaustion leaves the connection in the kernel backlog and pauses 10 ms before coordinator retry; normal cancellation/shutdown checks remain active. Socket reader references delay physical release and retain the charge. Service-token startup/reload reads share descriptor admission; reload exhaustion fails closed with 503. Request body length reserves native-byte capacity before reading and remains admitted through dispatch, with shared-holder clearing on exit. Response serialization reserves UTF-8 chunk upper bounds and simultaneous final copies, retaining final charges through writes and aliases. Byte-capacity rejection returns 503 before the affected handler or response publication. These payload policies do not cover all parser, escaping or native transport allocations.

resource.policy: Context checks before/after native operations; buffer data-lock waits poll at 50 ms; mapping population checks between writes of at most 65536 bytes and between initialization stages. Allocation, copies, sealing, mmap and physical cleanup are synchronous and not preemptible within a host operation. Logical close rejects new leases; admitted leases defer physical release. Failed cleanup retains ownership and charges for retry; ambiguous raw descriptor close is quarantined, never retried by descriptor number. Idle VM teardown reports unresolved cleanup. Explicit capacity limits are not wall-time or RSS guarantees. VM cancellation and GC checks remain per instruction. The single heap mutator lock may span at most 32 instructions, released around native/nested work and at every frame exit. Deferred resource cleanup runs after physical lock release at batch boundaries or frame exit; no wall-time fairness bound is claimed. Charged byte and read-scratch finalizers only mark pre-existing reservation state, without locking or queue allocation. Budget operations synchronously drain marked reservations under the ledger lock before their own updates. Charges can conservatively remain until a subsequent boundary; draining scans active reservations and has no wall-time bound. Failed drain preserves its pending state for retry. Explicit release remains synchronous.
